key_insight: An LLM coding-agent loop discovered ELOTE, a product-formula protocol that reduced median estimated T-gate cost by 85.35% while preserving chemical accuracy across 115 training molecular Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing product-formula structure and rotation-synthesis precision together could substantially lower fault-tolerant quantum chemistry resource requirements.
method: Run five independent agent searches, each with 100 code mutations, to optimize a shared protocol across molecules.
Minimize estimated T-gate cost for 95% success probability, subject to chemical accuracy for every training Hamiltonian.
Combine identical Pauli terms, use a first-order product formula, and tailor synthesis precision to coefficient magnitude, Pauli support, and diagonal character.
evidence_signal: Classical verification found chemical accuracy on all 115 training Hamiltonians (4–16 qubits) and 76 larger test Hamiltonians (18–22 qubits); a shared δ-ELOTE protocol for ten reaction energies cut geometric-mean cost a further 58.90% relative to ELOTE.
watch_item: Savings are classically verified resource estimates, not demonstrated quantum-hardware performance; applicability beyond the evaluated molecules and sizes remains unproven.
paper_title: Reducing T gates in product formulas with agent loops
